question: What is the primary mechanical role of the heart within the cardiovascular system?

options.B: To act as a pump distributing blood
options.D: To regulate core body pH exclusively

explanation: The heart functions as a muscular pump that drives blood throughout the entire vascular network to deliver vital substances. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is transported away from tissues by the cardiovascular system for elimination?
explanation: Metabolic byproducts like carbon dioxide are collected by the cardiovascular system and transported to the lungs for elimination from the body. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which layer of the heart wall is the thickest and responsible for the pumping action?
explanation: The myocardium is composed of cardiac muscle tissue and forms the thick middle layer responsible for generating the force needed to pump blood. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the endocardium?

options.B: To line the heart chambers and prevent abnormal clotting
options.C: To provide a fibrous outer protective covering
options.D: To anchor the heart within the mediastinum

explanation: The endocardium is a smooth endothelial lining that covers the heart chambers and valves to ensure blood flows smoothly without inappropriate clotting. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which valve separates the right atrium from the right ventricle?
explanation: The tricuspid valve is the atrioventricular valve located between the right atrium and the right ventricle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the chordae tendineae and papillary muscles?

options.A: To open the semilunar valves during systole
options.B: To prevent the AV valves from prolapsing into the atria
options.C: To generate the electrical impulse for heart contraction
options.D: To pump blood directly into the coronary circulation

explanation: Chordae tendineae and papillary muscles anchor the AV valve flaps to prevent them from blowing backward into the atria when the ventricles contract. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: When does the majority of coronary blood flow to the myocardium occur?
explanation: Coronary vessels are compressed during systole, so most myocardial perfusion takes place during ventricular diastole when the heart muscle relaxes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h4)

question: Where do the coronary arteries originate?

options.B: The base of the ascending aorta

explanation: The right and left coronary arteries branch directly off the base of the ascending aorta, immediately above the aortic semilunar valve. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which structure serves as the primary natural pacemaker of the heart?
explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node has the highest rate of spontaneous depolarization, making it the primary pacemaker that sets the heart rate. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the physiological significance of the delay at the AV node?

options.A: It prevents the atria from ever contracting
options.B: It allows the ventricles time to fill completely with blood
options.C: It speeds up the electrical signal to the Purkinje fibers
options.D: It initiates the repolarization of the T wave

explanation: The brief delay at the AV node ensures that the atria finish contracting and emptying their blood into the ventricles before ventricular systole begins. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h5)

question: What event directly causes the first heart sound (S1, or 'lub')?

options.D: Closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves

explanation: The first heart sound (S1) is produced by the sudden snapping shut of the mitral and tricuspid (AV) valves at the beginning of ventricular systole. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: During which phase of the cardiac cycle do the ventricles contract with all valves closed, causing pressure to rise without volume change?
explanation: Isovolumetric contraction occurs when the ventricles start contracting with all four valves closed, causing pressure to spike without any change in blood volume. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: How is cardiac output (CO) calculated?

options.A: Stroke volume divided by heart rate
options.B: Heart rate multiplied by stroke volume

explanation: Cardiac output is the volume of blood pumped per minute, calculated as heart rate times stroke volume (CO = HR x SV). [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: What does the Frank-Starling law of the heart relate to preload?

options.A: Increased stretch of muscle fibers leads to a stronger contraction
options.B: Higher arterial resistance decreases the stroke volume
options.C: Faster heart rate decreases the filling time

explanation: The Frank-Starling law explains that greater filling (preload) stretches cardiomyocytes, leading to a more forceful contraction and increased stroke volume. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: Which blood vessels act as the primary resistance vessels that regulate systemic blood pressure?
explanation: Arterioles possess significant smooth muscle in their walls, allowing them to constrict or dilate to control blood flow and resistance into capillary beds. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)

question: What structural feature do medium and large veins possess to prevent the backward flow of blood against gravity?
explanation: Veins feature one-way valves that work alongside skeletal muscle contractions to push low-pressure blood upward toward the heart without backflow. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)
